title: Building AIE: Open Q&A and Feedback Session with swyx
talk_summary: This is an open Q&A/feedback session about running the AI Engineer conference, covering logistics, expo layout, workshop registration, the mobile app, and speaker selection. It contains essentially no engineering technique for building AI agents; the only transferable ideas are meta-process lessons about scoping, iteration, and tooling.

takeaways.technique: Freeze scope to optimize process before scaling
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of growing the event, they explicitly commit to same size/venue next year so the team can fix known operational defects with a stable baseline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: next year we're not growing. So next year, same size, same venue, same everything. And we just optimized.

takeaways.technique: Open data + let users build their own client
takeaways.what_they_do: They publish all conference data as JSON with MCP/CLI access so attendees can vibe-code their own app instead of waiting on a vendor app.
takeaways.evidence_quote: why don't I just publish all my all my JSON files... there was nothing stopping you from vi coding your own stuff because the the data was open

takeaways.technique: Capture feedback as a requirements doc from live sessions
takeaways.what_they_do: They record the feedback session and treat the complaints as the literal requirements document for next year's rebuild.
takeaways.evidence_quote: everything that you just reported, we were recording this session. Those become the the sort of requirements document
